name: Digital Forensics & Incident Response
tagline: Analyze memory, disk, carved files, artifacts, and timelines from your own systems, lab evidence, and incident-response cases you legally possess.

tools.name: Volatility 3
tools.desc: The de-facto memory forensics framework: plugin-based analysis of RAM dumps (raw, EWF, crash/hibernation) across Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android — process listing, network artifacts, injected code, and more.
tools.when: Start here with any memory dump from a lab box or captured incident host; run pslist/pscan, netscan, and malfind to build the runtime picture.

tools.name: Volatility 2
tools.desc: The classic Python 2 framework (archived but stable) with the deepest plugin ecosystem and profile-based analysis for older Windows, Linux, and macOS dumps.
tools.when: Reach for it when a legacy or niche image lacks a Volatility 3 symbol table, or a plugin you need only exists in the classic tree.

tools.name: MemProcFS
tools.desc: Mounts a memory dump or live target (PCILeech FPGA/LeechAgent) as a virtual filesystem of processes, registry, and artifacts, with a batch forensic mode and YARA scanning.
tools.when: Fast interactive triage of a Windows dump without plugin CLI gymnastics, or live acquisition during your own incident response.

tools.name: Autopsy
tools.desc: GUI platform built on The Sleuth Kit: opens images and live drives, recovers deleted files, and runs ingest modules for web history, keyword search, and carving inside a case workflow.
tools.when: First-pass interactive examination of a drive or memory-card image from your own casework or a lab exercise — ingest everything, then drill into findings.

tools.name: The Sleuth Kit
tools.desc: Command-line suite for raw/EWF images: mmls for partition layout, fls/icat to list and extract inodes, istat for metadata, and tsk_recover for file recovery — the engine under Autopsy.
tools.when: Scripted or headless analysis, or when you need precise inode-level answers Autopsy hides behind its GUI.

tools.name: dc3dd
tools.desc: Forensic fork of GNU dd adding on-the-fly hashing, split output, pattern wiping, and detailed logging — evidence-grade imaging of a source drive to a file.
tools.when: Capture a definitive image of your own drive or USB stick before analysis so you examine the copy, not the live evidence.

tools.name: Guymager
tools.desc: GUI forensic imager for Linux producing flat (dd), EWF (E01), and AFF images with multi-threaded, pipelined reads for fast verified acquisitions.
tools.when: Click-driven imaging with progress bars and check-verification when you prefer a window over dc3dd's command line.

tools.name: foremost
tools.desc: Header/footer and data-structure file carver (originally from AFOSI) that extracts JPEG, ZIP, PDF, and other signatures from raw images or drives via a configurable file-type table.
tools.when: Unallocated-space fishing: run it on an image or free-space carve to recover deleted files the live filesystem no longer lists.

tools.name: bulk_extractor
tools.desc: Scans any input byte-by-byte and extracts emails, URLs, credit-card numbers, JPEGs, and JSON to feature files — recursively decoding compressed or encoded blocks without parsing the filesystem.
tools.when: Rapid 'what is in this blob' extraction over images or wiped drives before deep filesystem analysis.

tools.name: scalpel
tools.desc: Filesystem-independent carver using a header/footer definition database — a fast rewrite of foremost's carving engine with tunable per-type carve-size limits.
tools.when: When you need per-type carve-size tuning or an alterative engine for a stubborn image carve beyond foremost defaults.

tools.name: PhotoRec/testdisk
tools.desc: Signature-based recovery of 440+ file formats plus TestDisk for partition-table repair and undelete; no filename reconstruction, but deep salvage on corrupted or reformatted media.
tools.when: Last-ditch recovery from a reformatted or damaged partition or thumb drive in your own hardware lab.

tools.name: plaso/log2timeline
tools.desc: log2timeline extracts timestamped events (filesystem, registry, EVTX, browser, application logs) from an image or mount point into a Plaso storage file; psort turns it into a filtered super-timeline.
tools.when: Build the master super-timeline of an image: collect once with log2timeline, then slice and filter per question with psort.

tools.name: Timesketch
tools.desc: Google's web front-end for collaborative timeline analysis: import Plaso output and search, filter, star, and annotate events in your browser.
tools.when: Turn a giant Plaso timeline into something huntable — collaborative review and annotation for your own case and lab reports.

tools.name: KAPE
tools.desc: Kroll Artifact Parser and Extractor: selects forensically useful artifacts (registry hives, EVTX, Prefetch, MFT, browser files) from a live device or mounted image, then parses them with bundled tools in minutes.
tools.when: Speed triage in your own incident response or lab: point it at a live Windows box or image and get parsed artifacts quickly; extend via community KapeFiles targets.

tools.name: Eric Zimmerman's Tools
tools.desc: Suite of focused parsers — RECmd/Registry Explorer, PECmd (Prefetch), LECmd (LNK), JLECmd (JumpLists), ShellBags, Amcache, MFTECmd — answering execution-timeline questions from individual artifacts.
tools.when: Deep-dive a targeted artifact set: ask 'what executed, when, by whom' via Prefetch, LNK/JumpList, Amcache, and registry traces.

tools.name: Velociraptor
tools.desc: Open-source endpoint visibility and collection platform: deploy lightweight agents, run prebuilt forensic artifacts and fleet-wide hunts via VQL, and pull process, disk, and registry data to a central server.
tools.when: Your own lab or home-network incident: stand up a server, install agents, and answer 'what happened on these hosts' with artifacts and hunts.
tools.install: download velociraptor binary from GitHub releases; run server and deploy agent

tools.name: UAC
tools.desc: Unix-like Artifacts Collector: no-install shell script collecting processes, users, logs, cron, running-file hashes, and bodyfiles from Linux/macOS/BSD/ESXi in order of volatility, packaged for handoff.
tools.when: Rapid live triage on a Linux box you're responding to — run from a USB or read-only medium and hand the archive to your analysis machine.
